---
title: "Adding a conformance case"
---

sasonr accepts a feature only when it reproduces output generated by SAS 9.4.
A **conformance case** is a small SAS program together with the output SAS
produced for it. Cases are compared offline, so day-to-day development never
needs SAS.

## Layout

```
tests/conformance/<area>/<case>/
  program.sas      # the SAS program (invented data, usually datalines)
  data/            # optional external files read with relative paths
  meta.yaml        # SAS version, generation date, SAS return code, tags,
                   # sha256 of program.sas
  expected/        # produced by SAS, sanitised
    datasets/      # every WORK data set as SAS-native .sas7bdat
    attrs.csv      # memname, varnum, name, type, length, format, informat, label
    put.txt        # PUT / %PUT output
    log_notes.txt  # key NOTE / WARNING / ERROR lines
    listing.txt    # procedure output (only when the case tests it)
```

Data sets are kept as `.sas7bdat`, not CSV or XPT: SAS writes IEEE doubles to
`.sas7bdat`, so values (including numbers stored with `LENGTH < 8`) are
compared bit for bit. CSV text and the IBM floating point of XPT are lossy.

## Writing `program.sas`

Start with a header comment:

```sas
/* functions/scan_negative: SCAN with a negative count counts from the right
   source: SAS 9.4 Functions and CALL Routines, SCAN function
   tags: scan, character */
data out;
  length s $20;
  input s $ n;
  w = scan(s, n, ',');
  datalines;
a,b,,c -1
a,b,,c 3
;
run;
```

* Make results observable: write them to a WORK data set (compared exactly),
  `PUT` them to the log, or produce procedure output.
* Cover one behaviour per case, with its boundaries: ordinary values,
  missing values (`.`, `.A`, `._`), zero, extremes, empty strings and
  trailing blanks.
* Programs that SAS rejects are useful too: `meta.yaml` records the SAS
  return code, and sasonr must then stop with an error as well.

## Generating the expected output

Run the program with SAS 9.4 in a fresh batch session, export every WORK
data set as `.sas7bdat` (see `tools/sas/dump_work_sas7.sas`), then sanitise:

```bash
python tools/sanitize.py <case-dir>
```

The sanitiser removes the SAS start-up block, licence information, host and
user names, dates, times and absolute paths, and refuses files that still
contain forbidden words. `tools/refresh_gold.py` automates these steps when a
SAS runner is configured; without SAS, open an issue with the label
`needs-gold`.

## Running cases offline

```r
devtools::test()                       # unit tests + a fixed sample of about 300 cases
```

```bash
Rscript tools/run_conformance.R                     # every case: summary report by area
Rscript tools/run_conformance.R --since origin/main # only the cases your changes can affect
Rscript tools/run_conformance.R --baseline HEAD~1   # print the cases whose verdict changed
```

One run gives both verdicts. Every case runs once with
`options(sasonr.strict = FALSE)`; the runner records each strict gate (an
approximate or unverified feature) instead of stopping there, and derives the
strict verdict from it: a case without a gate has the same verdict in both
modes, a case with a gate fails loud in strict mode. Only a gate that sasonr
itself would catch (error recovery) makes the runner repeat the case in strict
mode. `--out FILE.csv` writes the strict verdicts and `FILE-strict-false.csv`
the others; `--strict true|false` runs one mode only.

Every full run is archived locally under `.claude/results/<commit>/` (not in
git): the per-case results of both modes, the summaries and an impact map that
lists, per case directory, the package functions that ran and the registry
rows that were read. `--baseline <commit>` compares a run case by case with
the archived one and prints only the changed cases. `--since <commit>` diffs
`R/`, `inst/registry/` and the runner against that commit and runs only the
case directories whose recorded functions or registry rows changed, or whose
files changed; the other cases keep their archived verdicts. A change to the
runner, a new or deleted R file, a top-level statement, code that runs at
package load, or a name looked up at run time (such as `sas_f_<name>`) runs
every case. `tools/update_registry.R --archive HEAD` and
`tools/update_proc_registry.R --archive HEAD` rebuild the registries from the
archived run instead of running the cases again.

There are three test tiers. `R CMD check` runs the unit tests only (the
cases are not part of the package build). `devtools::test()` adds a smoke
sample: the first case of every function and format verification matrix, of
every function directory and of every other area. `tools/run_conformance.R`
runs every case and is the check before a release; set
`SASONR_CONFORMANCE=full` to make `devtools::test()` run every case too, or
`SASONR_CONFORMANCE=none` to skip the conformance tests.

Each case is compared on several layers: data sets (values and order),
variable attributes, `PUT` output, key log diagnostics and listing. When a
case fails, fix sasonr, never the expected output.
